title: Avin of Neshikya

paragraphs: Shabbat 121a relates that Rav Yehudah, Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba and Rav Chanan visited Avin. Couches were brought for Rav Yehudah and Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba, but none for Rav Chanan bar Abba, as Hyman calls him here. Rav Chanan found Avin teaching his son and said, “Avin the fool teaches foolishness to his son.”

notes.text: The story continues from Shabbat121a to121b. The visitors come to Avin’s house, and Rav Chanan rebukes Avin. The supplied notice calls him Chanan bar Abba; the complete primary account has Chanan bar Rava. That patronym discrepancy remains open.

No new whole primary scalar was supplied here. The earlier Shabbat121a–b consultation and Chanan barRava versus supplied barAbba discrepancy are inherited rather than newly verified. Hyman’s guests, couches and rebuke direction remain as the current English gives them; the old bracket identifying him with the guests is not restored. The supplied121a is retained alongside the inherited continuation span. No variants-work witness resolves the patronym and no new family binding is made.

The consulted Shabbat 121a–b names Rav Chanan bar Rava both when he comes to Avin’s house and when he is left without a couch. Hyman’s print first names Rav Chanan without a patronymic and later calls him bar Abba. Rashi explains that the couches were for sitting and that Rav Chanan, angry, meant to provoke Avin with his remark.
